skill.name: accessibility-check
skill.description: Review UI components and pages for accessibility issues using WCAG 2.1 guidance, including keyboard access, labels, contrast, focus states, and screen reader concerns.
skill.summary: Audit UI accessibility against WCAG 2.1 and provide prioritized fixes.
skill.author: Dami-Randle

content.value_statement: Accessibility defects can block users and create compliance risk. This skill reviews interfaces against WCAG 2.1 and returns prioritized fixes.
actual_capabilities: Review pages and components against WCAG 2.1 Level A and AA checkpoints.
Assess keyboard access, focus order, focus visibility, and keyboard trap risks.
Check semantic HTML, ARIA usage, labels, page language, and reading order.
Identify contrast, text resizing, images of text, and color-only communication issues.
Recommend fixes for alt text, form labels, contrast, and focus indicators.
Format results with compliance status, issue priority, passing criteria, and testing notes.
limitations: It does not run tools unless the host agent executes them.
It does not replace testing with users who rely on assistive technology.
It focuses on WCAG 2.1 guidance, not every legal standard or jurisdiction.
Suggested fixes may need project-specific design and engineering review.

use_cases.title: Review a Feature Before Release
use_cases.description: Check a new interface for accessibility issues before it reaches production.

use_cases.title: Audit Design System Components
use_cases.description: Evaluate shared components for labels, focus states, contrast, and semantic structure.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Create a structured WCAG review with issues, passing criteria, and testing notes.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a visible page or screen.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this page for WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility issues. Focus on keyboard access, labels, contrast, headings, and screen reader concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review for a reusable UI component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component for accessibility defects. Include WCAG criteria, severity, user impact, and specific implementation fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Against Manual Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review after keyboard or screen reader testing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these manual test notes to produce an accessibility audit. Separate confirmed failures, likely risks, passing checks, and follow-up tests.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a Release Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced triage across a full workflow before launch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this workflow for WCAG 2.1 AA readiness. Prioritize blockers, map each issue to affected users, and propose a release-safe remediation plan.

output_examples.input: Review a sign-in form before release.
output_examples.output: The audit finds partial WCAG 2.1 AA compliance. Priority fixes include adding a persistent email label, improving button contrast, and confirming visible focus.

output_examples.input: Check a dashboard page for keyboard access.
output_examples.output: The report flags missing skip navigation, unclear menu keyboard behavior, and weak focus indicators. It also lists passing heading and landmark checks.

output_examples.input: Summarize accessibility risks for a modal dialog.
output_examples.output: The review identifies focus trap risk, missing dialog naming, and unclear Escape behavior. Recommended fixes are ranked by user impact and release priority.

best_practices: Provide the page, component code, screenshots, and any manual test notes for better findings.
State the target WCAG level and user workflow before asking for an audit.
Verify suggested fixes with keyboard testing, screen reader testing, and automated checks.
anti_patterns: Do not treat automated accessibility scans as complete proof of compliance.
Do not ask for a generic pass or fail without sharing the interface context.
Do not ignore user impact when prioritizing accessibility defects.

faq.question: Does this skill run automated accessibility tests?
faq.answer: It can recommend tools and interpret results. The host agent must run tools such as Playwright or pa11y.

faq.question: Which WCAG version does it target?
faq.answer: The skill is written around WCAG 2.1 Level A and AA checks.

faq.question: Can it review component code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review markup, styles, ARIA usage, labels, focus behavior, and related implementation details.

faq.question: Can it replace expert accessibility testing?
faq.answer: No. It supports review and triage, but expert testing and assistive technology validation remain important.

faq.question: What inputs improve the audit?
faq.answer: Provide source code, screenshots, product context, target WCAG level, and manual keyboard or screen reader notes.

faq.question: Does it cover legal compliance?
faq.answer: It helps organize WCAG findings, but legal requirements depend on jurisdiction and should be reviewed separately.
